scope: Corollary 1.5 (Positive five-color badness) of the manuscript “The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable” (preprints/The-Euclidean-plane-is-not-five-colorable-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 158 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 607c2601b5ae655c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a constant δ > 0 with the following properties. (i) For every coloring c : R2 → {1, . . . , 5} and every normalized finitely additive left-invariant measure µ on all subsets of the plane-isometry group E(2), the invariant-mean badness satisfies p µ 5 (c) := µ {T ∈ E(2) : c(T−1 0) = c(T−1 1)}  ≥ δ, where R2 is identified with C. (ii) If c is a Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring with two linearly independent periods, then P(c(A) = c(A + U)) ≥ δ, where A is uniform in a fundamental parallelogram and U is an independent uniform unit direction. For any Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring, if the conditional square-table frequencies P c(AR) = c(AR + U) | AR + U ∈ [−R, R]2  (R > 1) converge as R → ∞, their limit is at least δ; here AR is uniform in [−R, R]2 and independent of U.
